summary: Akio Tanabe works in Indology and other fields. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1984 to 1993, served as an associate professor at Kyoto University (~1998–2016), and took a post at the University of Tokyo in ~2016.
Akira Fujieda was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1931–1935) and later served as a section head (班長) there from ~1949 to 1974.

Akira Hirakawa was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Shoson Miyamoto (~1937–1950), earning a doctorate in 1959. He held professorships at Tokyo (1954–1975) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996–2002).

Akira Miyaji specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history/archaeology. He completed his BA, MA, and DLitt at Nagoya University, where he became emeritus in ~2001. He also held posts at Hirosaki University (~1978–1987) and Ryukoku University (~2001–2014).

Akira Mukai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral coursework at Hokkaido University. He served as an assistant at Hokkaido University (attested 1978) and as a professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (attested 1999).

Akira Omine was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University (~1949–1958). He held appointments at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (~1966–1980), Ryukoku University (~1993–2000), and became professor emeritus at Osaka University (~1993–2018).

Akira Onda worked in Buddhist studies and other fields after studying at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1952). He served as a professor at Toyo University (~1962–1986) and held posts at Kawamura Gakuen Women's University (~1988–1995) and Tokyo.

Akira Sadakata is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1955–1959) under Akira Hirakawa and Hajime Nakamura, and at the University of Paris (1963). He served as associate professor and professor at Tokai University (~1971–2007).

Akira Saito is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikido Takasaki and earned a PhD from the Australian National University. He held professorships at Mie University, Tokyo (~2000–2016), and ICPBS (~2016).

Akira Shimada is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the College of Art, Delhi, under Rajeev Lochan and Daud Ali. He held posts at the British Museum and the State University of New York.

Akira Suganuma was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Toyo University (~1959–1962). He spent his career at Toyo University (~1962–2005) as assistant, associate professor, professor, and president (1991–1994).

Akira Takeda was a Sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1956). His career included posts at Tokyo Woman's Christian University (~1965–1979), the University of Tokyo as professor (~1979–1991), and Meikai University (~1991–2001).

Akira Yuyama was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied under Hirakawa, Tsuji, Basham, and de Jong. He served at ANU (1965–1973), directed the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1976–1996), and was a professor at Soka University (~1996–2021).
Akitoshi Saito is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served at Taisho University, where he is attested as a professor in 1982 and as professor emeritus in 2014.

Alan Fox specializes in philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed a PhD at Temple University (attested 1988) and has served as a faculty member in philosophy at the University of Delaware since 1992.

Alan Gerard Wagner specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Harvard University (attested 2008), where he was supervised by Parimal G. Patil and studied with Robert M. Gimello, Charles Hallisey, Carl Bielefeldt, and Masatoshi Nagatomi.

Alan Sponberg was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD from the University of British Columbia. He held academic posts as a professor at Princeton University (attested 1980–1987) and in religious studies at Stanford University (attested 1988).
Alan Watts was a writer and thinker in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He received his education at St Hugh's School and The King's School, Canterbury (~1928–1932).

Alasdair Urquhart is a philosopher who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1963–1967) and the University of Pittsburgh (~1968–1973). He held an academic post at the University of Toronto beginning in ~1973.

Alastair Gornall specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He completed a PhD at the University of Cambridge (~2008–2013) and held posts at SOAS University of London (~2015) and Singapore University of Technology and Design (~2016).
